code_angle.fx32_scale_note: Raw fx32 /4096 gives x/z at 1/4 of the task floats (0.5/7.0 vs 2.0/28.0) while y matches (0.400); the world vector is proportional under either scaling, so the projected angle is identical (29.996 deg raw vs 29.997 deg task floats). The angle, not the absolute scale, is the transferable code value.

honest_limits: (a) The DEFAULT BW2 camera position frames the enemy only — the player mon sits behind its plane — because effect scripts move the camera during play; the transferable code value is the DIRECTION angle through the camera basis, not absolute default-camera screen positions.

(b) Per-move spawn offsets and per-move camera moves are effect-script DATA, not readable C source in this slice — origins are BW2's attacker anchor + the measured art zones from PLAYER-VFX-MANIFEST-20261026.json (mouth/cannon/hand), labelled as adaptation, never claimed as BW2 script values.
(c) Pokemon's code names no per-species body-part origin; body parts come from the move's nature + measured art, labelled as such.
